gloss: on purpose, expressly, going out of one's way

definitions.gloss: expressly, specially, going out of one's way
definitions.explanation: Taking extra effort or trouble to do something that isn't strictly necessary. Often implies appreciation for the effort.
Intentionally doing something unnecessary or counterproductive. Used critically.

examples.japanese: わざわざ{来|き}てくれてありがとう。
examples.english: Thank you for going out of your way to come.

examples.japanese: わざわざ{電話|でんわ}しなくてもよかったのに。
examples.english: You didn't have to go to the trouble of calling.

examples.japanese: わざわざ{危険|きけん}なことをするな。

notes:
COMMON PATTERNS:
・わざわざ～てくれる (take the trouble to ~ for someone)
・わざわざ～なくてもいい (don't need to go out of your way to ~)
・わざわざ～する{必要|ひつよう}はない (no need to expressly ~)

NUANCE: When expressing gratitude, わざわざ acknowledges that someone made extra effort. In negative contexts, it criticizes unnecessary or unwise actions.

SIMILAR: {態々|わざわざ} is the kanji form but hiragana is more common.

SEE ALSO: {敢|あ}えて (daringly, purposely) is similar but emphasizes doing something despite difficulties or opposition.
